scopes.name: umbra
scopes.rule: Umbra depends only on the Penumbra interface and contains no OS, browser or vendor header (architecture overview, section 1, rule 1).

scopes.name: penumbra interface
scopes.rule: The porting contract is platform-neutral, sits below Umbra and is installed, so it may include only the standard library and itself: neither Umbra, Abseil, nor any port or platform header.

ports.rule: Ports depend on the Penumbra interface and their platform, never on each other (architecture overview, section 1, rule 2).

entries.rationale: The C++23 library headers and the C++ headers for C library facilities are available on every target toolchain. Whether a particular library feature may be used is decided separately by ADR-0013 and docs/cpp-features.md.
These are the ISO C headers that the C++ standard itself provides ([support.c.headers]). POSIX and OS headers such as unistd.h, pthread.h or sys/*.h are deliberately absent.

ADR-0009 adopts Abseil as the portable base library; it hides platform differences behind its own API. It is allowed in Umbra's internal code only: installed headers, including the porting contract, use the standard library alone, so embedders never need a matching Abseil.
Umbra modules may include one another's headers; the rules for each module's own includes apply to its files.
The Penumbra interface is the only route from Umbra to platform functionality (ADR-0002, ADR-0003).

scopes.name: umbra
scopes.rule: No Umbra target may reach a Penumbra port or a platform library, directly or transitively (architecture overview, section 1, rule 1).

scopes.name: penumbra interface
scopes.rule: The porting contract links no port, platform library or Umbra target.

ports.rule: A port may link its platform libraries and the Penumbra interface, but never another port (architecture overview, section 1, rule 2).

entries.rationale: Umbra modules may depend on one another; the walk continues into them so their dependencies are checked too.
The Penumbra interface is Umbra's only route to platform functionality (ADR-0002); the walk continues so a port linked through it is still caught.
ADR-0009 adopts Abseil. Abseil encapsulates its own platform dependencies (for example CoreFoundation for absl::time on Apple platforms), so the walk stops at its boundary.
CMake's portable thread runtime target, required on some toolchains for the standard library's own <thread> and <mutex>; it exposes no platform API to Umbra.
